summary: The cut's MECHANICS are right and re-measured here: 15 manifest additions with no deployed key while the 347 locked entries keep hash and flag, the five registry edits per class, the seventh boot banner, the build-info roster newest-first, claraWork_v7 actually wired to loadFaProposalInputsStepV7 with the estate's six-condition predicate and both grounds at the contract's argument orders, no packages/db and no apps/web file touched, no work_result construction site in any chatTurn, and the 41 + 83 unit cells green at exactly the counts the report gives. The SPEC gaps are all in the REFUSAL and STATUS halves of the three #1136 reads, where the contract tables were transcribed into frozen constants but not into reachable code paths: two mapped sentences can never fire (proven by driving the shipped mapper), one whole contract row has no implementation at all, and the CLR03 arm answers a READ with an unrelated authoring sentence. Two further items are roster deviations the orchestrator should rule on rather than defects of craft.

findings.title: The CLR10 tenant-masking sentence can never fire in read_payroll_posting_state or read_agreement_terms; the person is handed the raw 'queue scope is malformed'
findings.evidence: waveS-lane08-ticket1136.md sections 1 and 3 both carry the row: 'CLR10 (queue scope is malformed) | client_not_found | "I cannot find that client under your firm." This is also the answer for another firm's real client - that is deliberate, and a tool must not distinguish them.' The implementation keys that map on the TYPED REASON: packages/runtime/workflows/chatTurn.v23.reads.ts:196 (reason === "queue_scope_malformed") and :455 (if (reason === "queue_scope_malformed")). But the door raises it with NO detail payload: packages/db/migrations/0352_agent_read_twins_payroll_agreement.sql:686,690,692 and 0011_daily_loop.sql:3757,3761,3763 are all `raise exception 'queue scope is malformed' using errcode='CLR10';` with no detail=, and authoringRefusal (packages/runtime/workflows/chatTurn.v11.tools.ts:81-82) derives reason ONLY from detail.reason. Driven rather than reasoned: a probe cell run in packages/runtime against the SHIPPED chatTurn.v23.refusals.ts, with Object.assign(new Error('queue scope is malformed'), {code:'CLR10'}) and the module's own mapper, returned {"ok":false,"code":"CLR10","reason":null,"fix":null,"message":"queue scope is malformed","details":{}} - the mapper returned null and the door's internal wording was carried through to the model. The two cells that look like coverage, chat-turn-v23-tools.test.mjs:126 ('another firm's real client is answered IDENTICALLY to a missing one') and :244, assert only the CONSTANT's text; no cell drives the mapper. The same cut's tenancy modules key on the CODE instead (chatTurn.v23.tenancy.ts:181, :291, code === "CLR11") and are correct, so the fix is a shape this cut already uses.
findings.required_fix: Key both maps on the sqlstate (code === "CLR10") as well as on the reason, returning {reason: "client_not_found", message: ...}, and add a cell that drives governedRefusalV23 with a CLR10 carrying no detail - the exact shape 0352 and 0011 raise.

findings.title: read_payroll_posting_state has no payroll_not_read arm: a summary that was never read is answered status "posted"
findings.evidence: waveS-lane08-ticket1136.md section 1's refusal table carries TWO distinct rows for the no-blocked-row branch: 'no payroll_posting_blocked row AND an approved entry on the filing | NOT a refusal | report the entry: its date, its memo and its total. The run posted.' and 'no payroll_posting_blocked row AND no entry | payroll_not_read | "That payroll summary has not been read yet." Name the task's own status from clara.get_document_state, never a guess.' chatTurn.v23.reads.ts:169-192 collapses both into one: when blocked === null it reads clara.get_document_state and returns {ok:true, status:"posted", document_state} unconditionally. No entry is read, the two states are never distinguished, and the token payroll_not_read appears nowhere in packages/runtime (grep returns no hit; PAYROLL_POSTING_STATE_REFUSALS at :133-141 carries only not_permitted and client_not_found). The result type's own comment at :180-181 admits the ambiguity - 'the run either posted or was never read' - while the field the model reads says "posted". No cell covers it: the four payroll_posting cells in chat-turn-v23-tools.test.mjs (:68, :92, :109, :126) drive the input schema, the client wall, the door source pins and the refusal constants, none of them this branch. The prompt stanza cannot compensate; it tells the model to report what the tool returned.
findings.required_fix: Implement the contract's two branches: read the filing's approved entry, answer posted only when one exists (with its date, memo and total), and otherwise return the payroll_not_read refusal naming clara.get_document_state's own status. One cell per branch.

findings.title: Every not_permitted (CLR03) sentence the five read contracts specify is declared but unreachable; a refused READ answers 'That authoring action is not permitted in this session.'
findings.evidence: The contracts name a per-tool CLR03 sentence: 'I cannot read your firm's inbox in this conversation.' (1136 section 1), 'I cannot read this client's payroll in this conversation.' (section 2), 'I cannot read this client's documents in this conversation.' (section 3), 'I cannot read your firm's agreements in this conversation.' (1137 section 1), 'I cannot read this client's rent in this conversation.' (1137 section 2). All five ship as frozen constants (chatTurn.v23.reads.ts:133, :234, :391; chatTurn.v23.tenancy.ts:72, :213) and none is referenced by a mapper: every governedRefusalV23 map in the two modules returns null for CLR03, so the message falls through to authoringRefusal's own CLR03 literal at chatTurn.v11.tools.ts:86-88, 'That authoring action is not permitted in this session.' Driven: the same probe cell with {code:'CLR03'} returned exactly that message. Calling a READ an 'authoring action' is also wrong on its face. Every cell that touches these constants (chat-turn-v23-tools.test.mjs:126, :180; chat-turn-v23-tenancy.test.mjs:86) asserts the string's value, never that any refusal carries it.
findings.required_fix: Map CLR03 in each of the five reads to that tool's own sentence, or delete the five constants and record in the report that the estate's generic CLR03 sentence is what ships - but not both.

findings.title: read_payroll_settlement_state answers the panel's 'no run is waiting' sentence for a document-narrowed read that simply did not match
findings.evidence: waveS-lane08-ticket1136.md section 2's table separates the two cases: 'document_id named, no matching run | NOT a refusal | this run's net pay is either already settled or not yet posted - never guess which; point at read_payroll_posting_state for the posting half.' and 'runs is [] | NOT a refusal | "No payroll run is waiting on its bank payment." (the panel's own empty-state sentence, reused verbatim)'. chatTurn.v23.reads.ts:293-302 filters first and then sets empty_sentence: runs.length === 0 ? NO_PAYROLL_RUN_AWAITING_PAYMENT : null on the POST-filter list, so a client with three open runs, asked about one already-settled summary, is told that no payroll run is waiting on its bank payment. The cell at chat-turn-v23-tools.test.mjs:180 asserts the constant's text only.
findings.required_fix: Compute empty_sentence from the unfiltered door answer, and give the narrowed-no-match case its own status pointing at read_payroll_posting_state, as the contract row says.

findings.title: CLOSING-PLAN roster item 3 - the invalid_author / CLR44 correction - was not taken, and the plan's escape clause does not apply
findings.evidence: CLOSING-PLAN.md, 'What the cut carries', third bullet: 'One correction to a body being succeeded. packages/runtime/lib/prepayment-schedule-basis.ts:119 still documents invalid_author as "CLR10, and NEVER SHOWN" ... The module is inside the frozen closure and deploy-locked, so the correction rides the successor copy. If the cut finds the mapping already correct in the file it copies, it records that rather than claiming the fix.' Measured at HEAD: prepayment-schedule-basis.ts:119 still reads '/** CLR10, and NEVER SHOWN: the successor always has the actor, so this is a wiring error. */', and frozen-workflows.json carries that path with "deployed": true. The mapping is NOT already correct, so the escape clause is unavailable; the lane declined the item and recorded it as a successor contract instead (waveK-lane04-ticket1144.md, 'The one correction to a body being succeeded - NOT taken'). The reasoning is sound and its supporting measurement is confirmed here (grep -rn CLR44 packages/runtime returns nothing, so nothing behaves wrongly today), but this is one of the three items in a roster the plan declared closed.
findings.required_fix: Orchestrator ruling: either accept the deferral explicitly in the integration record and carry the successor contract to the mainline cut, or have the item taken. It should not pass as silently discharged.

findings.title: confirm_tenancy_rent_plan_revision returns an extra offer key the settled section 7.2 shape does not carry
findings.evidence: waveS-lane08-fix.md section 7.2 - the section that SETTLED the part-kind question by measurement - spells the return literally: 'return { ok: true, status: "revised", plan: rentPlanRevisionPart(receipt), replayed: receipt.replayed === true };'. chatTurn.v23.tenancy.ts:692-698 returns {ok:true, status:"revised", plan, offer, replayed}, adding the raw clara.wake_get_tenancy_escalation_revision answer. The addition is defensible - it is how the turn can say both figures out loud - but it widens a shape a fix round settled byte for byte, and no cell asserts the result's key set: chat-turn-v23-tenancy.test.mjs:374 shapes rentPlanRevisionPart in isolation.
findings.required_fix: Either drop offer to match the settled shape, or record the widening in the ticket report as a deliberate departure from 7.2 with its reason, as the lane did for its other departures.

findings.title: Two non-database conditions are dressed as CLR sqlstates the database never raised, and one reuses this cut's own tenant-wall code
findings.evidence: chatTurn.v23.reads.ts:432-439 returns the not_read_yet answer with code: "CLR11", and chatTurn.v23.tenancy.ts:152-159 returns not_a_tenancy with code: "CLR10". Neither contract assigns a code to either (1136 section 3: 'no banked pair | not_read_yet'; 1137 section 1: 'draft.agreement_class is not tenancy ... | not_a_tenancy'), and in this very cut CLR11 is what both tenancy reads map to not_found / client_not_found (chatTurn.v23.tenancy.ts:181, :291). isGovernedRefusalV23 (chatTurn.v23.refusals.ts:26) treats any /^CLR nn $/ as governed and renderable, so a surface or a later tool branching on the code will read 'the reading has not finished' as 'not in your firm'.
findings.required_fix: Give the two lane-own refusals a code that is not a door's sqlstate, or record in the report which sqlstate each was deliberately dressed as and why.

findings.title: Three rows of #1137's confirmation table are not rendered: CLR13 to in_flight, and the two CLR04 arms
findings.evidence: waveS-lane08-ticket1137.md section 3's table carries 'CLR13 | in_flight | an in-flight sibling holds this key.', 'CLR04 authority_lost | not_permitted | "Your membership of this firm is no longer active, so I cannot record a confirmation as yours."' and 'CLR04 insufficient_role | not_permitted | "Confirming a rent plan needs a bookkeeper or above."'. CONFIRM_RENT_PLAN_REFUSALS (chatTurn.v23.tenancy.ts:383-405) carries none of the three, so all three fall through to the door's own message; the module's doc comment at :372-381 names the CLR04 pair as a deliberate carry but does not mention CLR13. CONFIRM_RENT_PLAN_LADDER (:352-365) also names the token operation_in_flight where the contract writes in_flight. Unlike SPEC-K-L04-01 these tokens DO reach a mapper - 0353_tenancy_agent_twins_obo_confirmations.sql:1561,1579,1601,1615,1633 raise with detail=jsonb_build_object('reason',...) - so this is a rendering choice, not a dead path.
findings.required_fix: Either add the three sentences, or extend the module's existing 'deliberately absent' comment to name CLR13 as well, so the deviation is visible to the integrator.
